info.name: PAD Team 2 — World Service
info.description:
World Service (Gurschi Gheorghe, Go). Owns the persistent campus map: rooms, sections, resource node placement, zombie spawn points and section unlock state.

**Running it:** start the service with `go run ./cmd/server` in this repository, then run the whole collection. Every request asserts the status code the contract promises, so a green run means the service still honours it.

**Data:** the service seeds the campus `utm_campus` at boot. The Main Wing is open, the East Wing waits on `math_analysis` and the North Wing on `operating_systems`. The CRUD folders create and delete their own throwaway records, so the seeded campus survives a run.

item.name: 1. Map queries
item.description: What the Game Service reads on every cycle tick.

query.description: Set to false to include locked sections

item.name: Get the map including locked sections

request.description: The same call with `unlocked=false`, which stops filtering and returns every room.
Rooms with optional filters by `type`, `section_id` and `unlocked`. Used to decide where an action is possible.
One room. `unlocked` is derived from its section rather than stored on the room, so the two can never disagree.

request.description: Spawn configuration. Zombie statistics and behaviour belong to the Zombie Service; only the type ids live here.

item.name: 3. Section unlocking
item.description: How the campus expands when an exam is passed.

request.description: Every section with its unlock state and room count.

Unlocks the section mapped to the course, bumps the world version and publishes `section_unlocked`.

`trigger_id` is the `attempt_id` the Exam Service returned. The normal flow is the `exam_passed` event; this endpoint is the administrative path.

Returns **201** the first time and **200** on a replay.
The same `trigger_id` again. Answers 200 with `already_unlocked` true and publishes nothing, so a duplicated event cannot generate a second wing.

item.name: 4. Worlds
item.description: CRUD over worlds. Works on a throwaway world, so the seeded campus is untouched.

request.description: Creates a world. `world_id` is generated when omitted and the version starts at 1.
Every world.
One world, with its current version.
Renames the world and bumps its version.
Deletes the world with its sections, rooms, nodes and spawn points.
Confirms the cascade: the world is gone.

item.name: 5. Sections
item.description: CRUD over sections. `unlock_course_id` names the course that opens them.

request.description: Adds a section to the seeded campus.
The section just created.
Replaces it. The world it belongs to cannot be changed.

item.description: CRUD over rooms. The room is created inside the throwaway section above.

request.description: Adds a room to a section of the world. The section must belong to the same world, otherwise 422.
The room just created.
Replaces it. The world it belongs to cannot be changed.

item.name: 9. Event delivery
item.description: The exam_passed event from the Exam Service, delivered over HTTP until the message broker lands. Status codes are chosen for a caller that retries: 2xx settles the event, 5xx asks for it again.

request.description:
A passed exam arriving from the Exam Service. `attempt_id` is what the unlock path stores as its trigger, so the same event can be delivered again safely.

Returns **202** when this delivery generated the section, **200** when the wing was already open.

exec: // A fresh trigger per run, so the folder stays re-runnable.

request.description: What a broker does after a timeout. The same `attempt_id` is answered with **200** and `already_applied`, and nothing is expanded a second time.

request.description: Passing an exam that opens no wing is ordinary, so the event is acknowledged with **200** and `ignored` rather than rejected. Rejecting it would make a broker redeliver something that can never succeed.
**400**: the event is missing `attempt_id` and `course_id`, so there is nothing to apply.
